description_full: SBO AG manufactures and sells steel products worldwide. The company operates in two segments, Precision Technology and Energy Equipment. It offers high-strength non-magnetic steels and precision components; advanced additive manufacturing; service and repair; energy equipment, such as high-performance drilling motors; rotary steerable tools; circulation tools; and well-completion solutions. SBO AG was formerly known as Schoeller-Bleckmann Oilfield Equipment Aktiengesellschaft and changed its name to SBO AG in July 2025. The company was founded in 1862 and is headquartered in Ternitz, Austria.

R&D investment of 3% of revenue (limited) signals commitment to product development and talent.
financial_summary: SCHOELLER BLECKMANN OILFIELD is a small-cap energy business with a $556M market cap on $502M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -1% over the past three years — essentially flat, and a business treading water is rarely a path to compounding. Operating margins are contracting by -3.3pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.
Returns on capital run at 14% against a 8% cost of capital, a 6-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, with gross margins sitting at 32%.

The business throws off $25M in free cash flow — roughly 5 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.07× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.4× net debt/EBITDA, and thin 2.6× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 5.5% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 36% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

prof: ROIC of 14% earns above the cost of capital of 8.0%, but the 6pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.51).

growth: Revenue has compounded at -0.9% over 3 years.

own: Insiders own 36.4%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 28%.
It returns 5.5% a year to shareholders (2.5% in dividends).

That works out to $16K of free cash flow per employee.
